title: Anti-GBM disease

steps.tx: The definitive diagnosis of **Anti-GBM disease** is established on immunofluorescence microscopy by pathognomonic, intense, continuous **linear IgG** ribbon staining lining the entire length of the glomerular basement membrane. This ribbon-like pattern corresponds to circulating autoantibodies targeting intrinsic conformational basement membrane collagen epitopes.

vis.alt: RPGN Immunofluorescence Patterns: Linear IgG Deposition
vis.caption: Linear IgG ribbon deposition along glomerular basement membrane (StewardMD). Features: type IV collagen, alpha3(IV)NC1, COL4A3, 3, 4.

steps.tx: Pathogenic autoantibodies in anti-GBM disease selectively target the non-collagenous domain 1 (**NC1**) of the **alpha-3 chain** of **type IV collagen**. Because this specific collagen isoform is expressed almost exclusively in the basement membranes of glomerular and alveolar capillaries, clinical manifestations are strictly restricted to the kidneys and lungs.

vis.alt: Anti-GBM Disease and Goodpasture Syndrome Mechanism
vis.caption: Autoantibody targeting of alpha-3 NC1 domain of type IV collagen (StewardMD). Features: pulmonary hemorrhage.

steps.tx: Co-presentation of anti-GBM glomerulonephritis with life-threatening **diffuse alveolar hemorrhage** defines classical **Goodpasture syndrome**. Pulmonary alveolar bleeding is strongly provoked by environmental insults including tobacco **cigarette smoking**, volatile hydrocarbon solvent exposure, or concurrent pulmonary infections that disrupt the alveolar capillary endothelial barrier.

Pulmonary alveolar bleeding is strongly provoked by environmental insults including tobacco cigarette smoking, volatile hydrocarbon solvent exposure, or concurrent pulmonary infections that disrupt the alveolar capillary endothelial barrier.

right.title: Isolated Anti-GBM Disease
points: Pure renal involvement without lung signs
Equal risk of rapid renal failure

steps.tx: Immediate induction therapy requires urgent **plasma exchange** (exchanging **4** liters or **1** plasma volume daily or alternate days for **14** days) to clear circulating anti-GBM antibodies. Concurrently, high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone followed by oral **prednisone** and oral **cyclophosphamide** at **2** mg/kg/day halts de novo antibody synthesis.

steps.tx: Renal prognosis depends critically upon renal function at presentation: patients presenting with complete **dialysis dependence**, **100% cellular crescents** on biopsy, or serum creatinine > **5.7** to **6.8** mg/dL (> **500** to **600** mcmol/L) without alveolar hemorrhage rarely achieve renal recovery, warranting avoidance of toxic immunosuppression.
steps.say: Renal prognosis depends critically upon renal function at presentation. Patients presenting with complete dialysis dependence, 100 percent cellular crescents on biopsy, or serum creatinine above 5.7 to 6.8 milligrams per deciliter without alveolar hemorrhage rarely achieve renal recovery, warranting avoidance of toxic immunosuppression.

steps.tx: In double-positive cases exhibiting circulating anti-GBM antibodies alongside **MPO-ANCA** or PR3-ANCA, patients exhibit severe rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis with a remarkably high **relapse rate**. Unlike pure anti-GBM disease which rarely relapses, double-positive patients require prolonged and careful **maintenance immunosuppression** mimicking systemic ANCA-associated vasculitis.

rows: Extended maintenance with azathioprine or rituximab

steps.tx: Serial measurement of anti-alpha-3(NC1) antibody titers by **ELISA** monitors treatment efficacy until complete serological clearance is achieved. Successful suppression of autoantibodies within **2** to **3** months confirms remission, after which relapses are exceedingly rare unless secondary lung exposure triggers recurrent alveolar hemorrhage.
steps.say: Serial measurement of anti-alpha-3(NC1) antibody titers by ELISA monitors treatment efficacy until complete serological clearance is achieved. Successful suppression of autoantibodies within 2 to 3 months confirms remission, after which relapses are exceedingly rare unless secondary lung exposure triggers recurrent alveolar hemorrhage.

left.title: Clinical Sequence
points: Sustained serological negativity in 2 to 3 months

steps.tx: Patients reaching end-stage kidney disease can safely undergo **kidney transplantation** provided circulating anti-GBM antibodies remain completely undetectable for at least **6** months. Premature transplantation in the presence of active circulating antibodies triggers fulminant **hyperacute allograft rejection** and rapid destruction of the donor kidney.
